clue.text: Level with another in top spot perhaps

definitions.text: Level with another in top spot perhaps

parts.words: Level with another in top spot perhaps
parts.note: level reads the same both ways, and so does the phrase top spot, so the clue offers two examples of words that read identically backwards

explanation.surface: A sports table where one team draws level with a rival at the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Words or phrases that read the same forwards and backwards, such as level or top spot, are the examples given.

clue.text: In favour of blocking both sides of Afghanistan border

indicators.note: blocking says one piece sits in the way between others
both sides means the first and last letters of Afghanistan

parts.note: pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: A supporter obstructing crossings at the Afghan frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is an edging strip or surround, such as the paved area bordering a runway or stage front.

clue.text: Criminal's time being dominated by unfortunate past company

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece dominated by others sits below them

parts.note: ill can mean unlucky or unfortunate, as in ill fortune
ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a British company now gone

explanation.surface: A criminal's prison term is overshadowed by an unlucky past business.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI was a major British chemicals firm, taken over in 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlawful or forbidden by law is a criminal matter.

clue.text: Showbiz pair given unusual order to move elsewhere

indicators.note: an unusual order puts the pair's names the other way round from how they are always billed

parts.note: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo

explanation.surface: A TV double act receives an odd instruction to relocate.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a famous British television presenting double act, never billed as Dec and Ant.
explanation.definitionFit: To decant is to transfer liquid, or people, from one vessel or place to another.

clue.text: Wealth of foreign couple, it keeps being oddly ignored

indicators.note: keeps says the reworked couple holds the next letters inside
foreign suggests something strange, so the letters of couple are rearranged
ignoring the odd letters leaves the even ones of being

explanation.surface: An overseas couple's riches, while their existence is strangely overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges COUPLE into OPULCE, which 'keeps' EN, the even letters of 'being'.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is lavish riches or luxury, so great affluence.

clue.text: Land that's part of Shanghai, not separate on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A territory that belongs to Shanghai and is not detached from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Land that's part' as the definition, but 'part of' is the hiding signal; 'Land' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, so a land or nation.

clue.text: He's committed to track husband leaving hotel in South London?

parts.note: Lewisham is a district of south-east London

indicators.note: leaving says one letter departs from the hotel name

parts.note: Hilton is a hotel chain

explanation.surface: A dedicated athlete; a husband walks out of a hotel in south London.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewisham is a borough of south London; the racing driver is committed to the track.
explanation.definitionFit: The seven-times Formula One champion is devoted to motor racing circuits.

clue.text: Flyer that details cost of repairs to Oxford?

parts.note: an Oxford is a style of laced shoe
a bill sets out the charge for repair work

explanation.surface: A leaflet itemising what it costs to fix up Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the city, but it is a lace-up shoe; the repair bill for it gives the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African wading bird with a clog-shaped beak is a creature that flies.

clue.text: Crack scared lively young individual

parts.note: to spring can mean to split or crack, as a mast springs
chicken means cowardly or scared

explanation.surface: A fractured, frightened youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually in the negative 'no spring chicken', the idiom describes a youthful, sprightly person.

clue.text: Record centrally every month registrations for college

indicators.note: centrally tells us to take the central letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An admissions office logs college applications every month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrally' takes the middle letter of each of the five words: E, N, R, O, L.
explanation.definitionFit: To record a name on a register or list is to sign that person up, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Display of animalistic behaviour puts choir off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or disturbed, so the letters of puts choir are rearranged

explanation.surface: A choir walks out after witnessing some beastly conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals perform ritual displays to attract a mate, which zoologists call wooing rituals.

clue.text: In speech Pope's displaying naivety

indicators.note: in speech says the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: Innocent is the name taken by thirteen popes, so the pope's is Innocent's

explanation.surface: The pontiff's address reveals how naive he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is a lack of worldly experience, the guileless state also called purity of mind.

clue.text: Moles, extremely active and very visible in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: visible in says the preceding letters show up inside the next piece
extremely points to the extreme letters, first and last, of active

parts.note: only the outer letters of active are used; that the answer also runs backwards across active and is a coincidence with no indicator

explanation.surface: Moles in Northern Ireland are busy and easy to spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests burrowing animals; here moles are skin blemishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Naevi is the medical plural for birthmarks or skin blemishes such as moles.

clue.text: Goddess who enchants occasionally by movie's finale

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only every other letter of who enchants
the finale of movie's is its last letter

explanation.surface: A goddess who now and then casts spells is on screen at the film's end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of 'who enchants', H, E, C, A, T; the 'finale' of movie's adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this figure is the deity of witchcraft, crossroads and the moon.

clue.text: States has no right to expose divisions within the UK

indicators.note: has no means the following letter is taken out

parts.note: states are nations or countries

explanation.surface: States lacking the right to reveal splits inside Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Shires such as Kent or Yorkshire are administrative areas of Britain.

clue.text: Discard popular overture of Grieg in playing the violin

parts.note: to discard something is to scrap it
in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: an overture is the opening, so the first letter of Grieg

explanation.surface: A musician drops a popular Grieg overture from a violin recital.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraping is a mocking word for bowing a fiddle badly, a humorous description of string playing.

clue.text: Fellows ousting twin sons of banned Olympians, they're bullies

indicators.note: ousting says one pair of letters replaces another

parts.note: Russian athletes were barred from recent Olympic Games over doping
two sons, each abbreviated s
f is short for fellow, so two fellows give two of them

explanation.surface: Fellow athletes push out a banned pair from the Olympic team as thugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffians are thugs or brutes who intimidate others.

clue.text: Expressing sorrow as second vessel is almost at capacity

parts.note: mo is short for a moment or second
an urn is a vessel

indicators.note: almost means dropping the last letter

parts.note: something at capacity is full

explanation.surface: Someone is downcast because yet another container is nearly full.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sorrowful or grief-stricken is the plain synonym, as at a funeral.

clue.text: Admitting hospital resistance, open fancy new Kidney Unit

indicators.note: admitting says the reworked letters take others inside
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters of open are rearranged

parts.note: r is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A new renal department opens, taking in hospital patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' turns OPEN into NEPO; 'Admitting' puts H and R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephron is the basic filtering structure of the kidney, so its functional unit.

clue.text: Onset of laryngitis interrupts Prime Minister's toast

indicators.note: interrupts says one piece breaks into another

parts.note: Edward Heath was a British Prime Minister in the 1970s

indicators.note: the onset is the start, so the first letter of laryngitis

explanation.surface: A sore throat breaks into the Prime Minister's after-dinner toast.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was UK Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast drunk to someone's wellbeing is a raised glass to their good condition, as in 'your good health!'.

clue.text: Even-tempered just after losing case of impeachment

indicators.note: after losing means the word is taken once some letters are removed

parts.note: just means fair or equitable

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone calm and fair even after an impeachment is thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of calm, steady temperament is placid.

clue.text: Decay found in vegetable plant

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits within another

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
rot means decay

explanation.surface: Rot discovered in a vegetable crop.
explanation.definitionFit: The protea is a South African flowering shrub.

clue.text: Pause in output elsewhere viewed as regressive

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
in says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A slowdown in production somewhere else is seen as a step backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds PUTEL inside 'output elsewhere'; 'viewed as regressive' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lull or easing off in activity is a slackening, often said of rain.

clue.text: Sport heading for crisis? That's not original

parts.note: Formula One, written with a Roman numeral I, is a motor sport

indicators.note: the heading is the first letter of crisis

explanation.surface: Motor racing is approaching a crisis, and its recent seasons lack originality.
explanation.walkthrough: Formula One is written FORMULA I, with the Roman numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something following a set pattern or stock template lacks originality.

clue.text: Cancel book after second advance is withheld

indicators.note: withheld means held back, so this letter is taken out

parts.note: an annual is a yearly book
a can stand for advance

explanation.surface: Cancel a book deal after the second advance payment is not paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' says which A goes: the second one in ANNUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, so to revoke or abolish.

clue.text: Actor ever disposed to respond too emotionally

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters of actor ever are set out anew

explanation.surface: A performer who has always been inclined to hysterics.
explanation.definitionFit: To react more strongly than a situation warrants is to respond with excessive feeling.

clue.text: Overindulge English composer

definitions.meaning: to eat or drink to excess in one bout
Ronald ... was an English composer of light music, known for Sailing By

explanation.surface: An English composer is accused of excess.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronald Binge wrote Sailing By, the tune played before the BBC radio shipping forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: To overindulge is to have a spree of excess eating or drinking; the surname belongs to Ronald, a British composer.

clue.text: Refined lady's humane, in an open manner

indicators.note: refined means processed again, so the letters of lady's humane are reworked

explanation.surface: A cultured woman's kindness is shown without any embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting openly and without shame or embarrassment is the adverbial sense.
